title: Three-day Sherpa deploy playpad and escrow notes
content:
OVERVIEW:
This is a rough playpad for the 3-day Sherpa rollout (internal name: sherpa-serp-optimizations). Goal: stage traffic across regions with progressive escrow thresholds, catch regressions early, and provide a compact rollback ladder. Working doc — lots of TODOs.

High-level goals:
- Canary in us-west1 then eu-west1, then global ramp over 3 days.
- Keep 99th p95 token latency < 220ms on baseline load (see telemetry gates).
- No more than 0.5% error rate increase vs baseline (5xxs + client errors).
- If quality regressions detected (auto-evals), pause ramp and trigger manual review.

Quick calendar (PST / UTC):
Day 0 (preflight) — 2026-05-10
- 08:00 PST / 15:00 UTC: Preflight standup (15m) — owners: Aisha, Ethan
- 08:30 PST: Infra dry-run, smoke tests (see checklist) — owner: Liam
- 09:30 PST: Final canary config push (traffic filters + quotas) — owner: Marisol

Day 1 (canary us-west1) — 2026-05-11
- 06:00 PST / 13:00 UTC: Operator handoff (30m)
- 06:30 PST: Enable 1% traffic to sherpa in us-west1
- 07:30 PST: Monitor 1.5h, evaluate telemetry gates, run small eval prompts (sample set A)
- 09:00 PST: If gates green, increase to 10%
- 12:00 PST: If still green, hold and sync with product (status note)

Day 2 (regional ramp) — 2026-05-12
- 06:00 PST: Enable eu-west1 canary at 2%
- Progressive increases every 3h: 2% -> 10% -> 25% across regions if gates pass

Day 3 (global roll) — 2026-05-13
- Gradual ramp to 100% over 6–8 hours with escrow thresholds and rollback windows at 25%, 50%, 75%

PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (before any traffic changes):
- [ ] Confirm infra images and runtime: PR#6789 merged and green. (Ethan)
- [ ] Load-test smoke: 5m baseline docgen at 2x expected QPS — watch OOM, GPU memory, backlog. (Liam)
- [ ] KV cache warmup script ready and validated in staging. (Marisol)
- [ ] Canary routing policies staged in routing service (config id: routing/sherpa-2026-05-10). (Aisha)
- [ ] Observability dashboards: latency/requests/error/quality eval panels pinned. (Ethan)
- [ ] SLO / alert review: ensure paging thresholds & on-call lists are updated. (SRE lead)
- [ ] Confirm hotfix build and rollback artifacts exist (tag: release/sherpa-2026-05). (Liam)
- [ ] QA runbook + eval prompt set A/B/C uploaded to Confluence linked above. (Marisol)
- [ ] Legal/compliance checklist for eu region (data residency) checked. (security)
- [ ] Communication templates prepared. (Aisha)

SMOKE TESTS & COMMANDS (run in staging before day0):
- Basic health: curl -fsS https://staging.redwood.ai/health || echo "HEALTH FAIL"
- Perf spot: python infra/tools/loadtest.py --target staging --qps 150 --duration 300
- KV cache warmup: scripts/cache_warmup.sh --model sherpa --seq 512 --workers 8
- Prefix caching check: curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/generate -d "{"prompt":"Hello world"}" -H 'x-test-prefix: yes'
- Small eval: curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/eval -d @eval_sets/setA.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST'

TELEMETRY GATES (auto-pass if all true in 90m window unless manual hold):
- Latency: p95 tokens < 220ms for model path; p99 < 420ms
- Errors: aggregated 5xx + 4xx increase < 0.5% absolute vs baseline
- Throughput: GPU utilization < 78% sustained; queue depth < 15 requests
- Quality: auto-eval score delta <= -1.5% relative to baseline on set A; if delta worse, set immediate hold
- Token-cost: cost-per-1000-tokens variation within +/- 12% expected (sanity check)

ROLLBACK LADDER (priority matrix):
- Scenario A: Severe latency spike (p95 > 500ms or p99 > 1s): immediate rollback to previous model variant in region (toggle routing to stable), alert on-call, open incident. (Action: rollback, then run hotpatch if infra)
- Scenario B: Error spike (5xx increase > 2% absolute): pause ramp, shift 100% of canary traffic back to stable, leave canary instances in read-only, capture traces.
- Scenario C: Quality regression flagged by auto-eval (delta <= -2%): hold and notify ML owner, capture sample outputs, run manual eval set B; if confirmed, rollback.
- Scenario D: Resource exhaustion (GPU OOM or infra capacity): scale down canary and spin up extra pool in dedicated with burst policy; if can't recover in 15m, rollback.

ESCROW ACTIVATION (if rollback must be slowed / users cannot be abruptly switched):
- Preconditions: executive signoff (product-engineering + SRE) and at least one fallback variant available for each affected region.
- Steps:
  1. Post to #release-ops with tag @here: "Activating escrow for sherpa rollout in us-west1 — holding at current traffic and diverting new sessions to fallback variant."
  2. Change routing policy: set escrow flag in routing/sherpa => mode=escrow, percentage=hold_pct (operator console).
  3. Start graceful drain timer (30m) for active KV caches to flush to persistent store.
  4. If escrow persists > 2h, trigger incident call and do deeper rollback plan.

COMMUNICATION PLAYBOOK (short templates):
- Slack (release-ops): "Day 1 canary 1% live in us-west1. Monitoring p95/p99. DM on-call for any 5xxs > 0.5%"
- Customer-facing (status page): "We are performing a staged rollout of sys improvements; minimal impact expected. If you notice regressions, please file at support.redwood.ai referencing ref REL-452."
- Internal incident pin: include links to dashboards + runbooks and note the commit/PR (PR#6789).

RELEASE NOTES (DRAFT) — keep short, product-friendly:
Title: Sherpa: response-optimizations and ranking tweaks (gradual rollout)
When: 2026-05-11 to 2026-05-13 (staged)
Summary: This release adjusts the response-routing and token handling for the sherpa family of LLM variants. Expected benefits: lower median latency for short queries (~8–12% improvement), improved ranking consistency for edge-case prompts.
What changes:
- Model change: sherpa-v2-small -> sherpa-v2-opt (quant+kernel selection tuned)
- Routing: per-request latency-aware routing enabled for small workloads
- Config: default max_tokens lowered from 2048 -> 1024 for interactive routes (opt-in for long-running jobs)
User impact: most customers will see faster short-query responses; heavy long-sequence workloads could hit shorter default limits (config opt-out available).
Known issues:
- Rare quality drift in zero-shot multi-step prompts (investigating — see REL-453).
- Some eu region config propagation lag observed in staging (mitigated).

POST-RAMP (first 48h) checklist:
- [ ] 6h post 100%: run full eval set C and collect auto-eval metrics. (Marisol)
- [ ] 24h: cost telemetry review (per-token economics), capture anomalies (Ethan)
- [ ] 48h: run retrospective: what throttles/escrows triggered, any manual rollbacks, produce a short retro (Aisha)

NOTES TO SELF / OPEN ITEMS:
- TODO: Add precise runbook pointers for 'promote-to-dedicated' scaling action — who owns cost approvals? (finance loop)
- TODO: Confirm fallback variant image tag names and ensure they are in the same subnet for fast routing.
- Check whether quota bump is needed in eu-west before 25% ramp.
- Consider adding an active hedging experiment for p99 latency (follow-up PR).

ATTACHMENTS & REFERENCES (internal):
- Eval sets: /confluence/RELEASE/eval-sets (setA/setB/setC)
- PR: runtime#6789 (merged)
- Tickets: JIRA-REL-452 (rollout plan), JIRA-REL-453 (quality investigation)

If anything looks off or you're reading this late — ping me in slack @aisha (slow hours may mean I won't respond immediately).

-- end of playpad (working draft)
